title: Remove and reinstall the rear wheel
summary: Learn the safe sequence for releasing a thru-axle rear wheel, clearing the derailleur and protecting the brake rotor.

tools.name: Correct hex key for the thru axle

steps.title: Shift to the smallest rear sprocket
steps.instruction: Before touching the axle, shift the chain onto the smallest cassette sprocket. This reduces derailleur tension and gives the wheel more clearance.
steps.why: A straighter, less-tensioned chain makes wheel removal and reinstallation easier.
steps.check: Chain is on the smallest rear sprocket.

steps.title: Release the rear thru axle
steps.instruction: Support the wheel and loosen the rear thru axle with the correct interface. Withdraw the axle while keeping control of the wheel.
steps.why: The axle locates and clamps the rear wheel in the frame.
steps.warning: Do not let the wheel drop while the axle is being withdrawn.
steps.check: Axle is fully released and controlled.

steps.title: Move the derailleur clear
steps.instruction: Pull the rear derailleur body gently backward while lowering the wheel out of the dropouts.
steps.why: The derailleur and chain wrap around the cassette and otherwise obstruct the wheel.
steps.warning: Do not force or twist the derailleur sideways.

steps.title: Lower the wheel out
steps.instruction: Guide the wheel down and away while keeping the rotor clear of the brake caliper and the cassette clear of the chain.
steps.why: The rotor is thin and easily bent; controlled removal prevents impact against the caliper or frame.
steps.warning: With a hydraulic disc brake, do not pull the brake lever while the wheel/rotor is removed.
steps.check: Wheel is free and rotor has cleared the caliper.

steps.title: Inspect before reinstalling
steps.instruction: Check the rotor for obvious bends, confirm the axle threads are clean and align the chain with the smallest sprocket before guiding the wheel back into place.
steps.why: Reinstallation is easiest when the drivetrain and brake are aligned before the axle is tightened.
steps.check: Rotor enters the caliper slot cleanly and wheel is seated before axle tightening.
